Explain strict grammar and AST allowlisting, and why syntax validation alone does not ensure safe execution.\",\"securityFocus\":\"security-hardening\",\"complianceStandards\":[\"OWASP-Top-10\"],\"language\":\"python\",\"riskTolerance\":\"low\",\"analysisScope\":[\"input-validation\",\"error-handling\",\"logging-monitoring\",\"dependency-security\",\"configuration-security\"],\"securityRequirements\":[\"Avoid eval and exec for untrusted input; use a restricted mathematical parser and evaluator with explicit operator, function, and variable allowlists.\",\"Reject attributes, imports, arbitrary calls, indexing, comprehensions, and other unsupported syntax; fail closed.\",\"Limit input length, AST node count, nesting, numeric literal size, exponent magnitude, intermediate result size, CPU time, and memory to prevent denial of service.\",\"Handle division by zero, domain errors, overflow, and non-finite results safely.\",\"Validate variable names and numeric values, isolate evaluation contexts, and prevent cross-user state leakage.\",\"Provide OWASP references and security tests covering valid arithmetic, injection attempts, malformed syntax, and resource exhaustion.\"],\"includeCodeExamples\":true,\"includeMitigations\":true,\"includeTestCases\":true,\"prioritizeFindings\":true,\"outputFormat\":\"detailed\",\"includeReferences\":true}"}]}
